_comment: Carry destination for the un-landed half of #1668 (D8-s3-01,
(handoff/r9-f5-config-text-1) fixed the other five findings in its
lane (N-escape, N-service-icons, the 9 bare-unit I5 leaves, the
Swedish Sensor-Gap Advisor mistranslation, the I5 curve-bias and
quick-setup wording) but left this one unfixed: the rename it needs
stage: the round-9 PR that closes #1668, the energy/accuracy entity-name-sort split for D8-s3-01

carries.from: R9-F5.1 (handoff/r9-f5-config-text-1): the config-text lane's PR, scoped to strings.json / translations/en.json / translations/sv.json / icons.json only
carries.control: Established by measurement with its null control. The D14 sweep (S6, commit 6b65c9c4a8, tools/audit/round9/D14/sweep/entity-family-name-sort-split/) enumerated 8 production-symbol-defined entity families and found 2 with an unexplained split under both the English and Swedish name sort: the accuracy family (sensor.PredictionAccuracySensor + button.DiagnoseIntervalButton, sensor.py/button.py) and the energy-meter family (sensor._AccumulatingSensor's 6 subclasses: Space/DHW/Total x Energy/Cost, sensor.py); the null control is the other 6 families (ecl110, tariff, learning, pv, card_headline, dhw), which the same enumerator reads as 0 unexplained splits in every ordering, because their members already share a translation-key lead token. F5.1's own attempt to fix the energy-meter half is the concrete instance that this is not a strings-only fix: renaming just the 6 entities' strings.json/translations/{en,sv}.json names to share a lead token (tried: "Lifetime <original name>") made `tests/entities.py`'s README-sensor-table completeness check fail (6 rows documented-not-built, the 6 renamed entities built-not-documented) and 6 of its sensor-existence checks raise KeyError (README.md and tests/entities.py both hardcode the pre-rename English names in ~16 places total). The rename was reverted before commit; it is not in this PR's diff.
carries.remeasure: Do not trust this paragraph's counts: they are measured at F5.1's merge base (db878b2) and this stage is judged against its own. Re-run `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub /path/to/python tools/audit/round9/D8/s3/m3_families.py` from an export of the D14 evidence commit (`handoff/audit-r9-evidence`, `tools/audit/round9/`) at your merge base and confirm `families_split_unexplained_name_en=2, _name_sv=2` still holds for accuracy and energy-meter before starting, and `=1, =1` after fixing only one of the two (the script's own `--perturb` flag demonstrates the accuracy-family fix in memory). Before renaming, `grep -n` the exact current English/Swedish entity names (README.md's sensor table, and every `by_name["..."]` / literal name string in tests/entities.py) so the rename's full blast radius is known up front rather than discovered one test failure at a time.
carries.brief: Closing #1668 needs both families renamed to a shared lead token, not just one: the accuracy family (Prediction Accuracy sensor + Diagnose Last Interval button -- rename needs a token that reads sensibly for a button too) and the energy-meter family (the 6 accumulating sensors). Files touched: `strings.json`, `translations/en.json`, `translations/sv.json` (name only -- unique ids and translation_keys stay put, this is D8-s3-01's own weakened disposition), `README.md`'s sensor-table section (rewrite the affected rows under their existing group headings), and every hardcoded entity-name literal in `tests/entities.py` that names one of the renamed entities (sensor-existence checks, the `TOTAL_INCREASING` state-class check, and any other by-name lookup -- grep before editing, per remeasure above). No production `.py` behaviour changes; this is a names-and-docs-only PR, but it is NOT the config-text lane (F5) because of the README.md and tests/entities.py edits, which sit outside that lane's file ownership.

carries.from: R9-F8.3 (handoff/r9-f8-docs-3): this PR -- it renames both families to a shared lead token exactly as this brief specifies (en "Lifetime ..." / sv "Ackumulerad ..." for the six accumulating sensors; the accuracy family gains the "Prediction Accuracy " lead on both its sensor and its diagnose button), touches strings.json, translations/{en,sv}.json, README.md's sensor and button rows and prose, and every hardcoded literal in tests/entities.py, with the unique entity ids and translation_keys left in place (D8-s3-01's weakened entity_id disposition)
carries.control: Established by measurement at this PR's head against the base enumeration: tools/audit/round9/D8/s3/m3_families.py reports unexplained name_en 2 -> 0 and name_sv 2 -> 0 (base 2/2 measured pre-fix), with entity_id unexplained flat at 1 -- the weakened disposition, unchanged by design. tests/entities.py carries the #1668 family-run block (runs of family membership across the sorted roster, members homed in a second family transparent) with its own null control: reverting the button rename in memory returns runs to 2 and the check fires. The full suite is green at the head (doc_claims ALL 84, entities ALL 1986).
carries.remeasure: Re-run PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tools/audit/round9/D8/s3/m3_families.py at your merge base from the evidence export and confirm unexplained name_en=0, name_sv=0 (entity_id=1 is the recorded weakened disposition, not a miss). The discharge completes when this PR merges and #1668 closes; if the merge-base figure is not 0/0, the rename collided with a later main merge and the collision is a new finding, not this carry.
carries.brief: Nothing further is owed to this stage: the brief's file list is this PR's diff. Keep this file's first entry until the merge lands, because it documents WHY the F5.1 strings-only attempt failed (the README/entities blast radius) -- after the merge that history belongs to the PR body, and the file can retire with the issue.
